blocks.text: David’s declaration in verse 1 identifies the place for the LORD’s house and altar. It follows the altar David built on Ornan’s threshing floor after the census and plague, so the chapter begins by treating this location as the appointed site for Israel’s worship.

David gives Solomon the task of building the temple while devoting himself to its preparation: materials, skilled workers, leadership, and public support are put in place for the work. The chapter also gives a reason David himself will not build it: his warfare and bloodshed are contrasted with Solomon’s promised time of rest and peace. This explanation is stated in Chronicles but is not given in Nathan’s oracle in 2 Samuel 7, so both presentations should be allowed to stand rather than treating one as a replacement for the other.
